Diagnostics keep the program names grade.py and evaluator_audit.py, so saved output stays identical. Changes behavior on purpose. Old behavior: grade.py main caught only InputError and Inconsistent, so this error escaped as a Python traceback, exit 1, which this case's baseline_defect records up to the traceback header; the frames name interpreter-specific lines. New behavior: bench-tools prints grade.py: and Python's str() of the error, exit 2, as for every other input it cannot read. Rationale: a crate command reports a failed read or write as an input error and never prints a Python traceback. Compatibility impact: the exit status of these failures changes from 1 to 2; both implementations write nothing, and callers treat any non-zero exit as failure. Python 3.12 and 3.14 agree. Resolving issue: #238.

grade-map-cleanup-bridge-exit.reason: Adopt for #238, part of #156 (delivery plan, slice 8), porting grade.py validate, inventory, map and invalidate to bench-tools grade validate, inventory, map and invalidate, and evaluator_audit.py second to bench-tools evaluator-audit second. No caller moves; grade.py and evaluator_audit.py stay the production commands until slice 11 deletes them. Diagnostics keep the program names grade.py and evaluator_audit.py, so saved output stays identical. Changes behavior on purpose, only where the checkout's bench/tools/prune_workspace.py breaks its contract. Old behavior: grade.py imported prune_workspace from beside itself and called it in process, so the fixture's broken script never ran and the mapping succeeded, which this case's baseline_defect records. New behavior: bench-tools runs python3 bench/tools/prune_workspace.py --grading-work WORK --target TARGET --receipt RECEIPT --apply in the checkout and treats an exit or output outside its contract as a cleanup failure: it names the command, its exit and the tail of its output, exit 2, and keeps no grades. Rationale: the bridge keeps one cleanup implementation until #159 ports prune_workspace.py and removes it. Compatibility impact: none with the checkout's own prune_workspace.py, which every other case runs. Python 3.12 and 3.14 agree. Resolving issue: #238; #159 removes the bridge.

Diagnostics keep the program names grade.py and evaluator_audit.py, so saved output stays identical. Changes behavior on purpose, under decision grade-map-runner-identity-v2, which lists exactly what differs: runner.mapping in each receipt the mapping writes, and the receipt's SHA-256 wherever grades.json pins it. Old behavior: grade.py map wrote runner.mapping as runner_files(), the SHA-256 of the 23 runner files. New behavior: bench-tools writes runner.mapping as the version 2 runner identity grade prepare writes: {"version": 2, "files": the 23 runner-file hashes plus "rust/bench-tools": the running executable's SHA-256, "bench_tools": its rust_runtime.py pin, "execution_policy_sha256", "codex_catalog_sha256"}. The structured identity rule labels runner.mapping, and each pin of the receipt is checked against its bytes in each run, so both implementations compare. runner.prepared is still copied from the key. Rationale: the mapping runs the pinned executable, so the 23 Python files no longer identify the code that filed the grade. Compatibility impact: no tool reads runner.mapping, and the receipt keeps contract current-assessment-receipt/v1. Python 3.12 and 3.14 agree. Resolving issue: #238.

grade-map-unicode-16-digit-assessment-nu.reason: Adopt for #238, part of #156 (delivery plan, slice 8), porting grade.py validate, inventory, map and invalidate to bench-tools grade validate, inventory, map and invalidate, and evaluator_audit.py second to bench-tools evaluator-audit second. No caller moves; grade.py and evaluator_audit.py stay the production commands until slice 11 deletes them. Diagnostics keep the program names grade.py and evaluator_audit.py, so saved output stays identical. Records an intended difference from older interpreters. bench-tools reads the number of each assessment-N directory with pyunicode::parse_int, whose decimal digits are pytext's Unicode 16.0 table, generated from Python 3.14. Old behavior: grade.py's int() used the running interpreter's Unicode database. Under CI's Python 3.12 (Unicode 15.0), int() refuses U+16D74, so the mapping stops with a ValueError traceback, exit 1, and writes nothing, which this case's baseline_defect records with Python 3.12's result up to the traceback header; Python 3.10 (Unicode 13.0) misses 110 digits in the same way. Python 3.14 numbers the next assessment 5, as bench-tools does. New behavior: as Python 3.14. Rationale: one table for every interpreter. Compatibility impact: the mapping names every directory it writes assessment- and ASCII digits, so no saved assessment directory holds such a digit. Resolving issue: #238.
